question: How can Xiaopu, Claude Code, and Codex be compared under the same enforceable and observable budget without inventing vendor-internal counters?
frontier: retain v2 and wait for an authoritative Codex model-step event
replace model steps with a shared local-tool PreToolUse cap and gateway-controlled cumulative output-token cap
use wall time only and report all other compute as outcomes
selected: prospective v3 shared output-token, covered-local-tool, and wall-time envelope
reason: The v2 model-step field is observable in Claude assistant events but not in Codex exec JSON. Both current CLIs support a blocking PreToolUse surface for covered local tools, while a provider gateway can cap cumulative generated output. Wall-time-only matching leaves a large compute confound; inferring Codex steps is asymmetric.
anti_harking_boundary: v3 was defined after inspecting the three-task v2 pilot; v2 outcomes must not be pooled into v3 confirmatory statistics
residual_risks: Codex documents that hosted and specialized tools may bypass the local hook path
the shared provider gateway has only an offline fake-upstream test and is not live-validated
a live hook smoke test still requires an authenticated model call
next_action: install the gateway and shared hook into isolated comparator containers, then run one authenticated non-scored live smoke per CLI before spending on the 18-task slice
